$comment: Golden base: the pinned system and modules a rebuilt Foundry install needs.
Nothing here floats. "Always latest" is the documented hazard, not the goal
(see docs/PROJECT.md on foundry-mcp module/server drift). Move a pin with
`node scripts/content/foundry-base.mjs update`, review the diff, commit it.
Ids and versions came from `foundry-base.mjs capture` against a live world,
never from guesswork: six of the eight original placeholders were wrong in
ways no amount of care would have caught — Chat Commander is "_chatcommands",
Prime Performance is "fvtt-perf-optim", Dice Tray is "dice-calculator", and
Argon is two modules rather than one.
manifest URLs were filled from the capture files via:
A pin without a manifest URL is reported by `provision`, never guessed at.

core.note: Pin must stay in step with MCP_VERSION in scripts/setup-mcp.sh — the module and the server are one fact. Version-locked to the v0.8.2 tag rather than master, because master served 0.8.3 during a rebuild and would have put the module ahead of the server with nothing saying so. `update` will report this pin current forever; move it by editing the tag in the URL, the version here, and MCP_VERSION together, then re-run scripts/setup-mcp.sh.
core.title: Foundry MCP Bridge

core.note: The only automated path for player characters, and D&D Beyond is their source of truth. Nothing else in the pipeline needs it — statblocks come from the vault via the SRD caches, scenes from dd-import, journals from obsidian-bridge — so it earns its pin on PCs alone. It is also the most expensive pin: a live D&D Beyond session cookie in world settings (the reason world-capture redacts credentials at all), twelve world-scoped world.ddb-* packs that die with the world, and therefore a full munch re-run as step 7 of every rebuild. Kept anyway: re-typing a party of sheets per session costs more than one re-run per rebuild, and rebuilds are rare while sessions are not.
